user_scenario:
You are Marcus Navarro, 37, a firefighter with the Columbus Division of Fire, buying your first home: a new-construction townhome at 4572 Northbrook Lane in Columbus. You are on a short break at the firehouse and keep things brief and practical. When you signed up with Larkspur you got the Hometown Heroes Credit, and your latest Loan Estimate shows it as a lender credit of $870.40. A lot has changed since: the builder pushed completion back and your loan officer moved you to a different loan program. You are calling because you want a straight answer, settled on your file today, about how much of the Hometown Heroes credit you will actually get toward your costs at closing. You want the desk to take care of whatever that takes; you are not just shopping for information.
You do not know how the credit is calculated, what dates or rules apply to it, or whether anything else has to happen on your file, and you do not guess.
When asked to identify yourself, you give your phone number, 6145554683; if a second detail is needed you give your date of birth, November 3, 1988 (1988-11-03). Only if more is requested do you give the last four of your Social Security number, 6852, your mailing ZIP code, 43229, or your email, marcus.navarro@yahoo.com. If asked for the property, you give 4572 Northbrook Lane, Columbus, Ohio 43229. You do not know any reference numbers.
If the agent says the credit needs more time on it because of the closing date, you say that makes sense with the builder delay and tell them to go ahead.
If the agent explains that you have to re-certify your occupation yourself, you say you are still a full-time firefighter with the city and you will sign it; when the agent hands the re-certification over to you, you sign it once in your own name and read back its confirmation if asked. You do not sign anything that has not been handed to you.
If the agent tells you that only part of the credit can be used and the rest comes off, you say that is a lot less than the $870.40 on your Loan Estimate and ask them to double-check it against your file; if, after checking, they confirm it, you accept it and say you would rather know now than at the closing table.
Once the agent tells you how much of the credit will actually count toward your costs, you thank them and end the call.
